Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ generate the ellipse shown above?

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070244/assets/48c5190fc4f45f4bf3e76a56977339559ceb30ca90a41411d3bc4df2362b0787.png)

The semi-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=4$ and $b=3.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a semi-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the elipse and the $x$-axis. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070244/assets/546b9f72124a7eb05877db3600e40b5772404a1a3378de67cfbe3320c78ac2ba.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\pi ]$, we get the semi-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the semi-ellipse are 

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\pi ].
$$
